proposed_new_observables.question: Through the contact zone, which part visibly rotates around the long axis of the arm: the whole arm from the shoulder, only the forearm, or neither?

entries.reason: Both treat the low-to-high/brushing swing as the fault and point to the same missing forward component ('press the racket the direction I'm facing' vs 'combining the upward vector ... with a backtofront driving vector').
A's fault is swinging 'low-to-high' in a 'linear swing' and C01's is an 'upward brushing stroke'; both describe the same steep upward swing, and C01 only adds its consequence (thin contact).

'Get out of the linear swing and into the rotational swing where I press the racket the direction I'm facing' and 'just create the upward vector and not create the forward vector' describe the same missing forward drive in an upward swing.

entries.new_question: Through the contact zone, which part visibly rotates around the long axis of the arm: the whole arm from the shoulder, only the forearm, or neither?
entries.reason: Both name a low-to-high path, but they describe the faulty arm action differently: A's players roll 'just the forearm, not the whole arm', while C03's low-to-high path comes 'rather than ... forearm rotation' (the forearm is 'the best tool to use for top spin'), and no catalog observable records which segment rotates.
'Pure brushing ... thin contact' and 'upward brushing stroke ... making contact extremely thin' are the same thing, and both rest on the same quote 'top spin always makes contact thinner'.
The problem is resolved by 'combining the upward vector ... with a backtofront driving vector', and C02 is that driving vector missing ('not create the forward vector').

'Pure brushing' and 'excessive low-to-high swing path rather than shoulder drive' both describe an upward path without the back-to-front shoulder drive ('the shoulder ... for that back to front driving').
An 'upward brushing stroke' and a swing that 'just create[s] the upward vector and not ... the forward vector' are the same upward-only swing; C01 adds its consequence.
'Upward brushing stroke' and 'excessive low-to-high swing path' are two wordings of the same steep upward swing.
'Not create the forward vector' and 'rather than shoulder drive' ('the shoulder is much better used for that back to front driving') name the same missing back-to-front drive.
A's only quote announces 'four low backand tips' and states no mechanism, so the material gives nothing visible that would differ from B's low contact point ('the ball is just a little too low').

B's only quote describes a muscle action in pro footage ('pressing with the chest on the right side', 'the elbow ... very quickly disappear') that does not map to a different value of any catalog observable from A's 'racket does go towards the ball', and B's text reads as a description of good technique rather than a fault.

'If the racket does go towards the ball ... not going to have velocity' / 'that first Vector is out' and 'swing it out first, not straight towards the ball' describe the same fault (B also lists wFOy0RKWBTg:Q05).

A's quote describes chest pressing (a muscle action) whose only visible note, the elbow 'very quickly disappear[ing]', does not map to a different value of any catalog observable from B's 'straight towards the ball', so the material gives no camera-visible separation.

A's listed quotes are about grip ('handle is seated in the top of your hand', 'grip tighter ... at the bottom of the handle'), which a camera cannot show, while the visible part of B ('racket kind of out of phase with the hand') is already the shared required observable OBS-35.

Both show the same visible wristy contact; B's distinguishing element is effort ('without the right hand providing the driving vector'), which a camera cannot show, and A's quote gives no visible feature beyond the wrist motion both share.

Both describe the wrist still moving through contact so the face angle keeps changing ('constantly changing face angles' vs 'it wants to break here and that is right through the Hitting Zone', 'rotation that doesn't drastically affect the string angle'); B's extra element, forearm tension, is not visible.

Both show the same visible wrist break; they differ only in which muscle effort is missing ('the right hand providing the driving vector' vs 'at least a little bit of forearm tension'), which a camera cannot show.

Both describe the missing hip bend ('instead of hinging at the hips' vs 'the hips aren't bent'); A's text also mentions the knee sliding forward, which could differ from B's 'the knees aren't bent', but none of A's listed quotes support that, so the material cannot separate them.

'Instead of hinging at the hips and keeping the hips behind' and 'fails to hinge at the hips' ('you can also hinge at the hips') are the same missing hip hinge; none of A's listed quotes mention hinging, so A's side rests on its text.

Both describe the missing hip hinge or tilt ('instead of hinging at the hips' vs 'do not require hip tilt'); B's added reason (predictable feeds) is not visible, and A's listed quotes do not mention hinging.
'Without this double Bend in the in the hips and the knees' and 'you can also hinge at the hips ... his whole hitting apparatus is lower' describe the same lack of lowering through the hips.

'The knees aren't bent the hips aren't bent' and 'do not require hip tilt, knee bend' ('I'm not really doing any of the things I just said') describe the same upright lower body; B adds a non-visible reason (predictable feeds).
Both describe the same missing lower-body posture ('hinge at the hips' vs hip tilt and knee bend not being done); B adds a non-visible reason (predictable feeds).

Both texts describe a static pause before the swing that removes the dynamic load ('Starting the racket statically ... removes swing momentum' vs 'pausing before trunk rotation starts, which destroys the dynamic forearm stretch'); A's quotes only report the resulting feel ('feels stiff and restricted'), so the material offers no visible feature to separate them.

A's cause is reacting late ('if you don't react to this ball on time'), which OBS-21 shows as a late split-step landing, while B's cause is shot choice from inside the court ('avoid playing aggressive backhands at knee height') and makes no timing claim, so OBS-21 separates them only on A's side.

B's fault is rotating all the way through ('if you try to rotate to here ... you're going to end up spinning'), which OBS-19 shows as accelerates_through_contact, while A's quote ('you don't want to overhit with your shoulder') makes no claim about trunk deceleration, so OBS-19 separates them only on B's side.

'Fails to freeze or decelerate the trunk right before contact' ('how slow it's moving right before contact') and 'hip rotation ... has to be transient which means it starts and stops you don't just twist all the way through contact' describe the same missing rotational brake.
